title: Hidden Passages of Paris: Palais Royal & Wine Tasting
summary: Wander Paris's glass-roofed 19th-century passages—from Palais Royal to Passage Verdeau—then unwind with wine and cheese at a cozy local bar.

description:
passages couverts built in the early 1800s, when covered shopping arcades were the height of urban innovation. This tour takes you through five of the finest surviving examples, each with its own character, history, and hidden details.

We begin at the Palais Royal, once a royal residence and revolutionary hotbed, now a peaceful arcaded garden ringed with boutiques and Daniel Buren's striped columns. From there we slip into the Galerie Vivienne, widely considered the most beautiful of all the passages, with its mosaic floors, neoclassical reliefs, and sweeping glass ceiling.

Crossing toward the Grands Boulevards, we enter the Passage des Panoramas, the oldest covered passage in Paris (1799) and once home to the city's first panorama rotundas. It's a maze of stamp dealers, engravers, and small restaurants that still feels frozen in the 19th century. Next door, the Passage Jouffroy greets you with a wave of warm air from the old heating system and leads past antique shops, the Musée Grévin wax museum entrance, and a beloved vintage toy store.

Finally, we cross into the Passage Verdeau, the quietest and least touristed of the five, favored by collectors of old postcards, cameras, and rare books. It's the perfect place to slow down and notice details the crowds miss.

The walk concludes at Juicy Wine Bar, a relaxed, unpretentious spot where a curated wine and cheese tasting awaits. Your guide will help you pair a selection of French wines with regional cheeses while you swap impressions of the afternoon — a fitting, unhurried close to a walk through Paris's hidden architectural history.

This tour is ideal for travelers who've already seen the Eiffel Tower and the Louvre and want a slower, more textured look at the city — equal parts architecture, history, and local flavor.

5. What Sets This Tour Apart (max 1000 characters)

Most Paris passages tours stop at one or two arcades and move on. This one is a complete circuit through five connected passages — Palais Royal, Galerie Vivienne, Passage des Panoramas, Passage Jouffroy, and Passage Verdeau — so you experience the full evolution of the passage couvert style in a single, walkable afternoon, without backtracking or long transfers between sites.

It's also the only version of this walk that ends with a sit-down wine and cheese tasting rather than a rushed photo stop. At Juicy Wine Bar, you get a genuine pause: a curated pairing, a place to rest your feet, and time to talk through what you just saw with your guide and group. It's part architecture walk, part local hangout — history you can taste.

description:
Journey through nearly 800 years of Parisian history on an immersive experience through the historic heart of the city.

Explore Île de la Cité with your guide and discover how this small island became the medieval centre of royal power and one of the most important places in Paris.

Begin with the story of the Palais de la Cité, the enormous medieval palace where French kings once lived and ruled. Walk through the historic surroundings as your guide brings medieval Paris to life, revealing stories of kings, royal ceremonies, religion, politics and intrigue.

Then enter Sainte-Chapelle, one of Paris's most extraordinary Gothic masterpieces. Built in the 13th century for King Louis IX, the royal chapel is famous for its spectacular stained-glass windows. Look closely at the hundreds of scenes depicted in the glass while learning how the chapel reflected the wealth, faith and power of the medieval French monarchy.

Continue to the Conciergerie, where the story of Paris takes a dramatic turn. Discover how the former royal palace became a courthouse and, during the French Revolution, one of the most notorious prisons in France. Learn about the Revolutionary Tribunal, the prisoners held there and the final weeks of Marie Antoinette before her execution in 1793.

Continue toward Notre-Dame Cathedral and discover more of Île de la Cité's historic streets, monuments and hidden corners. Your guide connects the landmarks around you to the wider story of Paris, from medieval royalty and revolution to the city of today.

Complete your experience with a relaxing Seine River sightseeing cruise. From the water, enjoy a different perspective of Paris and admire its famous landmarks, historic bridges and riverside architecture—a memorable finale to your journey through the city's royal and revolutionary past.

Follow your local guide through charming streets where medieval scholars once studied, writers dreamed of changing the world, and generations of Parisians lived, loved and created.

Along the way, enjoy fascinating stories, unexpected discoveries, local recommendations and beautiful places to photograph.

Come for Notre-Dame and the Panthéon. Leave with a little piece of Paris in your heart.
